summary.title: About
summary.content:
I enjoy building the part of the web people actually see and interact with every time they open a website or an application.

If backend developers are the musicians in a band, then frontend is the vocalist – the part the audience actually hears and remembers. From the user’s perspective, this “voice” is what shapes the entire experience of the product.

I focus on creating fast and lightweight websites and SPA applications with modern and creative design. Most of my work is built with React and Next.js, and I enjoy adding motion and personality to interfaces using GSAP. This website, by the way, is built with the same technologies.

As a professional Frontend Developer and UI/UX Designer, I can take full ownership of the visual side of a project – from the initial idea to the final interface.

frontend.title: Frontend
frontend.content:
I started my frontend career in 2021 after completing an internship at Purrweb. Since then, I have worked on commercial products including Radiant Metrics and Planyway. For the past two years, I have been developing Planyway and gradually migrating a large legacy application from Angular and JavaScript to React and TypeScript.

During this time, I have worked on calendars, timelines, filtering systems, reports, charts, workload planning, and other complex interfaces. I have built reusable components, virtualized lists, PDF, CSV and XLSX exports, API integrations, and performance improvements.

My work goes beyond writing code. I participate in requirements discussions, technical planning, risk assessment, and code reviews. I can take a feature from the initial idea all the way to release.

design.title: Design
design.content:
I have been designing commercial interfaces since 2021, often combining the roles of designer and frontend developer. Later, I studied interface design at Bureau Gorbunov, while most of my experience came from real projects, continuous practice, and feedback.

For me, design starts with understanding the product domain and its users: who they are, what they need to accomplish, and how they interact with the interface. Only then do I move on to structure, visual hierarchy, typography, and other visual decisions.

My frontend experience helps me design interfaces that can actually be built. I consider component states, responsive behavior, and technical constraints from the beginning, and I also have experience creating UI kits for large applications.
